    The Light Test

    By Lens 🔎 — a pocket check for card stock, and one of the oldest tells in the binder.

    How to do it

    Hold the card in front of a bright light or your phone flashlight and take the photo. Real card stock has a dark core and blocks the light — a dull glow at most. Thin fake stock glows translucent.

    In the checker, this photo is an optional extra after your front and back photos of a Pokémon card — take it when you can, skip it when you can't. A slab is sealed in its case and a plush has no card stock, so the light test belongs to loose cards.

    What you're looking at

    A dull glow at most: real card stock is built around a dark core layer, so bright light barely gets through. The card stays mostly dark — that is the stock doing its job.

    Glowing translucent: thin stock with no dark core lets the light pour through, and the art shows through like a lampshade. That is a tell worth writing down — one tell, on its own.

    Its honest limits — by Lens 🔎

    The light test reads the stock, not the art. A card can pass it and still be a reprint, or fail it and need a closer look. It's evidence, not a verdict.

    One tell among many

    The checkers never sign a verdict on one tell — the print, the lettering, the shine, and the stock all get read together, front AND back. The light test speaks only for the stock, so it rides along as evidence beside the rest: never a standalone verdict input, and never a pass/fail gate. In a check, skipping it never blocks anything — the front and back photos are the ones a verdict needs.

    The Light Test, taught by Lens 🔎

    Pip's Batch Check 🦊

    Line up your cards

    Up to 5 cards — say, one binder page — checked in one pass. Batching saves trips, never standards: every card gets its own category pick, its own front AND back photos, its own photo-quality gate, its own identity match, and its own signed verdict on its own record. No shared verdicts, no shortcuts.

    One free check pops per card, and only when that card's own verdict signs. A card whose photos bounce at the quality gate spends nothing — and the rest of the batch carries on without it.

    Card Condition Grader

    Its own window, its own job: scan a photo of your card — front and back — and get its condition graded: corners, edges, surface, and centering, on the standard scale from Mint down to Damaged.

    Condition is not real-or-fake

    Why?

    This grader reads wear only — it never says whether a card is genuine. A counterfeit can be mint and a genuine card can be beat up. For real-or-fake, that's the Checker's window, and it stays separate from this one.

    5 free condition grades to start

    The grader's own pool — separate from the checker's free checks, and never touched by them. A grade pops one only when it completes; a photo the grader can't read pops none. This demo never uses any up.

    Grade a card

    Lay the card flat, keep glare off it, and fill the frame — all four corners and edges in view on both sides, because that's exactly what gets graded. Out of a sleeve if you can; sleeves hide surface wear.

    The Donation Cauldron

    For Child's Play — sealed packs for kids, never cash

    Pokémon is hard for kids to get these days. We catch the fakes — and a slice of every upgrade puts sealed packs in kids' hands.

    🪙 0 in the potGoal 🪙 250,000

    • 5% of every upgrade builds the fund that pays for the packs.
    • The receipt and a photo get posted here every time a pot ships.

    The pot fills for real as coins are spent. A donation goes out only when the pot is full and the fund covers the full $25 — until then, nothing is promised and nothing is sent.

    Mini Games

    Five games live in the app — one shelf, one door. The rest moved to the website arcade; nothing was deleted.

    🫧 Each game gives you 3 free runs a day. After that, a practice run costs 🪙 10 — practice scores never post to any leaderboard, ever.

    Testing saves (right now): while this public test runs, every check is saved to the test pool automatically — photos and result, unverified — so the checker can learn. Test scans are never filed as verified, never added to the genuine-card library, and never used as graded test answers. Scan gates (full app, at launch): a scan joins the database ONLY if (1) you explicitly agreed first, AND (2) the card is verified — verified as legitimately genuine, or verified as legitimately fake (a confirmed fake counts). Inconclusive / unverified scans are never filed. If you do not agree, a scan is used for that one check only and is not kept.

      🪙 How coins work

      Your coins live on this device only, for now. They are never real money. When real sign-in lands, your coins move to your account — until then, nobody else's device can see your coins, and we cannot see theirs either.

      How you earn coins right now

      🎮 Games pay coins — the first clear of a level pays most: Bubble Beat 50 · Cauldron Match 30 · Mystery Bubble 20 · Match Audit 20 · Cardboard Stack 10 (+2 a rung crossed). 📅 Daily check-in pays +10. 🫧 Scanning a card pays +10. The five games that moved to the website arcade pay their coins over there.

      What coins buy now

      Treats and corner dressing for your pet (a small shelf, capped for good), practice runs past the free daily cap — whose scores never post — bonus tell-training packs, and pours into the donation cauldron. Coins never buy a check, a grade, a verdict, or a tier. That fence is permanent.

      Play & learn — practice with coins

      Every game on the shelf gives 3 free runs a day. Past that, a practice run costs 🪙 10 — and its score never posts to any leaderboard. The tell lessons themselves stay free forever; coins only ever buy more practice, never the lesson.

      The donation cauldron

      Pokémon is hard for kids to get these days. We catch the fakes — and a slice of every upgrade puts sealed packs in kids' hands.

      5% of every upgrade goes into the donation fund.

      Pour coins into the shared cauldron. When the community jar fills, the donation fund covers $25 of Pokémon product (at our cost), donated through Child's Play — games for kids in hospitals — and the receipt and a photo are posted right here, where everyone can see it. One fill is always that same $25 of product: coins never convert to money at any other rate, and the donation is always made by hand, never charged automatically. More cards into more players' hands.

      🪙 How coins work

      Your coins live on this device only, for now. They are never real money. When real sign-in lands, your coins move to your account — until then, nobody else's device can see your coins, and we cannot see theirs either.

      How you earn coins right now

      🎮 Games pay coins — the first clear of a level pays most: Bubble Beat 50 · Cauldron Words 25 · Cauldron Match 30 · Cauldron Cannon 30 · Mystery Bubble 20 · Match Audit 20 · Pop Path 25 (a full run) · Rapid Fire 15 (a full run, +1 a stage past the first) · Cardboard Stack 10 (+2 a rung crossed). Replays pay a smaller amount, and each game pays up to 150 coins a day.
      📅 Daily check-in — +10 coins
      🃏 Scan a card (front + back) — +10 coins per scan, max 50 a day from scans

      How it works

      1. Send your link to a friend.
      2. They open it and sign in with their name — you both get +100 coins, once per friend.
      3. When they buy their first coin pack, you both get +10 free checks.
      Inviting yourself doesn't count, and each friend pays out once. Bonuses land on this device, under the name you signed in with.
